page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Double-booked
title: Double-booked
description:
It's chaos at Tip Top Trading. Tom is in a panic and needs help! He has arranged more meetings than he can cope with and is going to have to face some unhappy clients. Anna decides to step in and help.
This episode explores language for offering help.
phrases: Is there anything I can do?
Can I give you a hand?
Give me a shout if you need anything.

listening_challenge.question: What does the company Citrus Ventures do?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: ‘Look forward to hearing from you soon. Kind regards, Anna.’

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: (on the phone) ... And Margery said: 'I don't think I've ever seen a vegetable quite that size before...'

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Where's that hole-punch?!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Ah, business as usual in the offices of Tip Top Trading.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh for goodness sake! What a disaster! I can't believe it!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text:
But one member of the team seems bothered.

Tom
Arrgh!

Narrator
Anna, this is the moment to show you’re willing to help.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Use phrases like 'Is there anything I can do?' 'Let me help!' or, to be more informal, you can say, 'Can I give you a hand?' or 'Give me a shout if you need anything!'

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Right.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Go on!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Are you okay Tom?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: (grumpily) No.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Is there anything I can do?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: (grumpily) No.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh. What's wrong?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Everything.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I see. Can I give you a hand?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text:
My computer has crashed. I've lost my phone. And there's a big, big problem with my timetable. I’ve got two meetings scheduled at the same
time with two extremely important clients. I can't do them both at once!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Let me help.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Thanks Anna, but these are big, big clients. They need someone of experience.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, give me a shout if you need anything!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I can handle this, alright?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: 'I can handle this'... ungrateful idiot. But you used all the right phrases Anna, well done. Anyway, I bet he'll change his mind.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Oooh, I know, and the purple ones are so much more powerful...

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Anna? Could you help me?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Ha! I told you so!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: They've both arrived at once! Oh god! I'll deal with Mrs Kumquat...

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: You talk to Mr Lime, he's from a company called Citrus Ventures. They own hundreds of juice bars.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Are you sure that's a good idea Tom?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I don't have much choice, do I?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Well I could

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text:
Just keep him occupied Anna, tell him how great he is... no, no, tell him how great I am. Find out what he wants. If it's about the - well, never
mind, just be nice.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Understood.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Mr Lime! Are you well?

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: Yes, but I'm actually rather angry too.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Ah, well let me introduce you to Anna!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Mr Lime, it's a pleasure to meet you! Let me help with your coat.

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: Oh er... Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Can I give you a hand with your scarf too, Mr Lime?

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: Oh... Thanks.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Now, please come this way and you can tell me what's wrong.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Well done! Anna used some good phrases to step in and help with this mess. Let's hear them again:
But Mr Lime is obviously upset about something. What is it? And how will Anna deal with the problem? Let's hope it doesn't end in disaster!
